page: Amazon Web Services c5d.18xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features dual Intel Xeon Platinum 8124M processors running at 3.4 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, providing 72 dedicated vCPUs across 36 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is configured at 144.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a 1:2 compute-optimized ratio of 2.0 GB of memory per vCPU. Local physical storage is directly integrated, delivering 1800 GB of high-speed NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a 25 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance contains zero discrete GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate significant compute capacity across highly parallelized workloads. The multi-core stress-ng metric reached 66669.07, and PassMark overall CPU scored 49974.67, both falling into the top 25 percent tier. Instruction set extensions, including AVX-512 and FMA, bolstered the PassMark CPU extended instructions benchmark to 66801.39, also ranking in the top quartile. Memory throughput is notable under large read operations, achieving 209.03 GB/sec uncached and 3706.44 GB/sec in cached small blocks. PassMark database operations scored 22233.59, supported by the balanced core architecture and NVMe storage access.

In contrast, single-threaded execution and AI text generation represent distinct performance tradeoffs. Single-core evaluations, including Geekbench single-core (1181.0) and stress-ng single-core (1424.29), remain within the median range. LLM text generation throughput drops into the bottom 25 percent, registering 52.33 tokens/sec on a small 135M model and 7.25 tokens/sec on a medium 7B model due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware. Multi-threaded decompression and compression tasks perform at median levels, with bzip3 reaching 62.42 GB/sec and gzip single-threaded handling 24.44 GB/sec.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the c5d.18xlarge yields high parallel compute density paired with integrated high-speed NVMe storage on a single bare-metal-equivalent Nitro envelope. The bundled 1800 GB NVMe SSD volume avoids external network storage overhead for temporary scratch space. This profile matches batch processing, continuous integration compilation pipelines, distributed databases, high-performance computing modeling, and data extraction pipelines requiring local caching.

The instance is not suited for large-scale language model text generation or graphics workloads given the complete absence of GPU accelerators. Workloads should focus heavily on CPU-bound parallelism, high packet throughput, and disk-intensive scratch operations, such as Clang software compilation, video transcoding, and clustered data manipulation.
description: Amazon Web Services c5d.18xlarge is a high-density, compute-optimized instance based on the Nitro hypervisor. Powered by Intel Xeon 8124M processors on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 72 dedicated vCPUs (36 physical cores at 3.4 GHz) and 144.0 GB of DDR4 memory, matching a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The configuration includes 1800 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local instance storage and 25 Gbps baseline networking, without GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place its multi-core processing in the top 25 percent, with strong showings in PassMark CPU (49974.67), extended instructions (66801.39), and uncached memory read bandwidth (209.03 GB/sec). However, single-core metrics and LLM token generation remain average to weak due to CPU-only execution. The instance offers resource efficiency for compute-intensive tasks requiring fast local scratch disks, such as distributed compilation, batch processing, data extraction, and relational database hosting.
